title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz · The Discovery of Oz, the Terrible
description: A great Voice fills the throne room, until a little dog tips over a screen.

characters.name: Oz, the Great and Terrible
characters.role: A great Voice from the dome · then a little old man, in the same throat

characters.name: Dorothy
characters.role: A little girl from Kansas · the one who asks

characters.name: The Scarecrow
characters.role: Stuffed with straw · a light, dry voice

characters.name: The Tin Woodman
characters.role: Made of tin · a hard, ringing voice

characters.name: The Cowardly Lion
characters.role: A very large Lion · a low voice, and one roar

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: I am Oz, the Great and Terrible. Why do you seek me?

cues.speaker: dorothy
cues.text: Where are you?

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: I am everywhere, but to the eyes of common mortals I am invisible.

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: I will now seat myself upon my throne, that you may converse with me.

cues.speaker: dorothy
cues.text: We have come to claim our promise, O Oz.

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: What promise?

cues.speaker: dorothy
cues.text: You promised to send me back to Kansas when the Wicked Witch was destroyed.

cues.speaker: scarecrow
cues.text: And you promised to give me brains.

cues.speaker: tin-woodman
cues.text: And you promised to give me a heart.

cues.speaker: lion
cues.text: And you promised to give me courage.

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: Is the Wicked Witch really destroyed?

cues.speaker: dorothy
cues.text: Yes. I melted her with a bucket of water.

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: Dear me, how sudden!

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: Well, come to me tomorrow, for I must have time to think it over.

cues.speaker: tin-woodman
cues.text: You’ve had plenty of time already.

cues.speaker: scarecrow
cues.text: We shan’t wait a day longer.

cues.speaker: dorothy
cues.text: You must keep your promises to us!

cues.speaker: lion
cues.text: (The Lion gives a large, loud roar. Toto jumps, and tips over the screen in the corner.)

cues.speaker: tin-woodman
cues.text: Who are you?

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: I am Oz, the Great and Terrible.

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: But don’t strike me, please don’t, and I’ll do anything you want me to.

cues.speaker: dorothy
cues.text: I thought Oz was a great Head.

cues.speaker: scarecrow
cues.text: And I thought Oz was a lovely Lady.

cues.speaker: tin-woodman
cues.text: And I thought Oz was a terrible Beast.

cues.speaker: lion
cues.text: And I thought Oz was a Ball of Fire.

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: No, you are all wrong. I have been making believe.

cues.speaker: dorothy
cues.text: Making believe! Are you not a Great Wizard?

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: Hush, my dear. Don’t speak so loud, or you will be overheard, and I should be ruined.

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: I’m supposed to be a Great Wizard.

cues.speaker: dorothy
cues.text: And aren’t you?

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: Not a bit of it, my dear. I’m just a common man.

cues.speaker: scarecrow
cues.text: You’re more than that. You’re a humbug.

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: Exactly so! I am a humbug.

cues.speaker: dorothy
cues.text: But I don’t understand. How was it that you appeared to me as a great Head?

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: That was one of my tricks. This I hung from the ceiling by a wire.

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: I stood behind the screen and pulled a thread, to make the eyes move and the mouth open.

cues.speaker: dorothy
cues.text: But how about the voice?

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: Oh, I am a ventriloquist.

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: I can throw the sound of my voice wherever I wish, so that you thought it was coming out of the Head.

cues.speaker: dorothy
cues.text: I think you are a very bad man.

cues.speaker: oz
cues.text: Oh, no, my dear. I’m really a very good man, but I’m a very bad Wizard, I must admit.
